newsitem.title: USA: Forecaster raises U.S. Northwest runoff estimates.
newsitem.headline: Forecaster raises U.S. Northwest runoff estimates.

text.p: The Northwest River Forecast Center, in its March update, slightly increased forecasts for spring runoff at most hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest.

The Portland, Ore.-based center, part of the National Weather Service, forecast January-July runoff on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam at 134 percent of average, compared with its "early-bird" March forecast of 133 percent.
Last year, runoff at The Dalles during the same period was 132 percent of average, near 140 million acre feet (maf).
The January-July inflow forecast for the Lower Granite reservoir on the Snake River in Washington was increased to 161 percent of average from 159 percent in early March.

April to July inflow to the Brownlee reservoir on the Snake River in Idaho was forecast at a revised 103 maf or 178 percent of average rates, down slightly from the early March forecast of 181 percent.
